title: Word Families and Root Words
keyIdea: A word family is a group of words built on the same root word, so they share a meaning as well as letters: act, actor, action, react and active are all about doing. Prefixes such as re-, un- and dis- go in front of the root and change its meaning; suffixes such as -or, -ion and -ive go after it and change its job, from doing word to thing, person or describing word. The root's spelling can shift a little (solve, solution, insoluble), and a word that only shares letters, like cactus, is not in the family. Peeling off the prefix and suffix to find a root you know is a quick way to work out a new word.
familyTip: Pick a root at dinner, such as play, help or kind, and take turns adding a part to make a real family word: player, playful, replay, unhelpful, kindness. Then try a trap: is kindle in the kind family? Talk about how you can tell.

visual.caption: In the help family, or only shares letters? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build words on act, sort look-alikes out of the family, match the solve family to clues, peel off parts to find roots, and file words by job.

kid: A root word is the main part of a word. Help is a root. You can add bits to it. Helper, helpful and unhelpful are all in the help family.
A prefix goes at the front, like un- or re-. It changes the meaning: unhelpful means not helpful. A suffix goes at the end, like -er or -ful. It can change the job of the word: a helper is a person.
Family words share a meaning, not just letters. Helmet starts with h-e-l, but it is not about helping. So it is not in the family.
Sometimes the root changes a little. Solve becomes solu- in solution. It is still the same family. When you meet a long new word, peel off the front and the end. Do you know the root?
adult: Ages 7 to 9. In England this is the Years 3 and 4 programme: pupils apply their growing knowledge of root words, prefixes and suffixes to read aloud and understand new words, and use word families based on common words to show how words are related in form and meaning (solve, solution, solver, dissolve, insoluble is the curriculum's own example). In the US it matches Common Core L.3.4c (use a known root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word with the same root) and leads into L.4.4b (Greek and Latin affixes and roots).

A root, or base word, carries the core meaning. Prefixes (re-, un-, dis-, in-) usually change meaning; derivational suffixes (-or, -er, -ion, -ive, -ness) usually change word class, so one family can supply a verb, a noun, a person and an adjective. The root may change spelling between related words, as in solve and solu-, or happy and happi- in happiness.

The test for a family member is shared meaning that comes from a shared root, not shared letters. Fact, tractor and cactus contain a-c-t but come from different roots, and kindle is not related to kind. Morphology helps both reading and spelling, which is why it is taught alongside phonics.

Common mistakes: putting a word into a family because it shares letters; adding any prefix or suffix to any root without checking a real word results (unact, actful); thinking a spelling change means a different family; and mistaking a prefix or suffix for the root when breaking a word down. In the lab your child builds words on act, sorts look-alikes, matches the solve family to clues, peels words to their roots and files a family by job.

practice.prompt: Which word is in the same family as help?
practice.hint: Which word is about helping, not just spelled with h-e-l?
practice.explain: Helpful is help + ful, full of help, so it shares the meaning. Helmet and hello only share letters.

practice.prompt: Zara has {n} word cards. She says cactus is in the act family because it has a-c-t in it. Is she right?
choices: No: cactus is a plant, it does not mean doing
Yes: it has the letters a-c-t
Yes: every word with act is in the family
practice.hint: Family words share a meaning as well as letters.
practice.explain: A cactus is a plant, so it does not share the meaning of act. It only shares letters, so it is not in the family.

practice.prompt: What is the root of rebuilding?
practice.hint: Peel off the prefix at the front and the suffix at the end.
practice.explain: Re- is a prefix and -ing is a suffix. What is left, build, is the root, and it carries the meaning.

practice.prompt: Max finds {n} words in the solve family. Which one fits: “It will not dissolve”?
practice.hint: In- at the front means not.
practice.explain: Insoluble means not able to dissolve: in- means not, and solu- is the solve root. A solver is a person and a solution is an answer.

practice.prompt: Which word names a person who acts?
practice.hint: Which suffix names a person who does something?
practice.explain: The suffix -or names a person, so an actor is a person who acts. -ion makes a thing and -ive makes a describing word.

pool.prompt: Which word is not in the kind family?
pool.hint: Which word only shares letters with kind?
pool.explain: Kindle means to light a fire and comes from a different root. Kindness and unkind both keep the meaning of kind.

pool.prompt: What is the root of disagreement?
pool.hint: Peel off dis- at the front and -ment at the end.
pool.explain: Dis- is a prefix and -ment is a suffix, so the root is agree. Disagreement means not agreeing.

pool.prompt: Solution is spelled with solu-, not solve. Is it in the solve family?
choices: Yes: solu- is the same root, spelled a little differently
pool.hint: Does solution share the meaning of solve?
pool.explain: A solution is the answer you get when you solve something. The root changes spelling a little, but it is the same family.

pool.prompt: Which word was built by adding a prefix to act?
pool.hint: A prefix goes in front of the root.
pool.explain: Re- in front of act makes react, to act back. Actor and action add a suffix at the end instead.

pool.prompt: Lily tries {n} endings on act. One gives actful. What is wrong?
choices: Actful is not a real word: not every part fits every root
She put the suffix in front
pool.hint: Say it. Is it a word you have heard or read?
pool.explain: A family word must be a real word with a meaning. Act + ful does not make one, so pick a part that fits, like -ive: active.

pool.prompt: Tom says tractor is in the act family. Why is he wrong?
choices: Tractor comes from a root meaning pull, not do
pool.hint: Check the meaning, not only the letters.
pool.explain: Tractor only looks like act. It comes from a root meaning pull, so it is not about doing and not in the family.

pool.prompt: Ben has {n} create words. Which one describes something?
pool.hint: Which suffix makes a describing word?
pool.explain: -ive makes a describing word: a creative idea. A creator is a person and a creation is a thing.

pool.prompt: What is the root of unbreakable?
pool.hint: Peel off un- at the front and -able at the end.
pool.explain: Un- and -able are a prefix and a suffix. The root is break, so unbreakable means it cannot be broken.

pool.prompt: Which word is in the same family as invent?
pool.hint: Which word shares the meaning of making something new?
pool.explain: An invention is a thing someone invents, so it is in the family. Inside only shares letters, and vent is a different word.
